title: Randy the Whip, Larry McKinley and Club Tijuana
summary: Looking at a 1953 Courier page, Tex remembers a classmate DJ, Larry McKinley and Club Tijuana, and mentions a planned book.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Anything else from his column strike you?

Well, there are many things that strike me when I start thinking about my classmate from Hawthorne High School, Randy the Whip, who was one of the first disc jockeys in the city of New Orleans. He was really a mechanic by trade. He had a mechanical mind. And he taught school at a big building on the corner of Jackson Avenue and doing Chapitula Street for many years. And then he left there and he became a disc jockey and started doing broadcasting on the radio. And he also was a good friend of Frank Pena because Frank used to, if he didn't call me, he would call Randy whenever he had some kind of shows. And then when I think about Larry McKinley here, his first name is really Alvin. I had forgotten about that. And then I wrote this years ago, you know. And there are many other things that strike me when I think about Club Tijuana, which was Mr. Bolin.

Right. And his daughter later took the club over today. It's a shadow of the past that was the glory of Club Tijuana at South Saratoga near Calayo. And incidentally, I passed through there about five or six months ago and I took pictures of the place the way it is today because I'm contemplating on working on a book sometime this year with the help of the good Lord. Well, some of this material will be utilized and you will be given your credits. No doubt about it. Well, I've got to, Ted, because you've got to remember that you and me, we've been together for quite some time trying to highlight the beauty of what music, jazz, in order to add another dimension to the, not only to the archives, but to the image of New Orleans from a standpoint of quality information about who was who and what was what in the city of New Orleans at one time in history and what it is today. And you're a younger man than I am. And so then we look down here at the Million Dollar Room, which was owned by Mr. Curry.
